title: QuickBooks Expands Connector in Claude and Plugin in ChatGPT with New Sales Invoicing, Payroll, and Lending Features
summary: QuickBooks is bringing actionable sales, payroll, and lending intelligence to Claude and ChatGPT. Create invoices, look up payroll details, and benchmark loans through conversation.
body_text: Intuit Blog All Posts Innovative Thinking Tech Innovation QuickBooks Expands Connector in Claude and Plugin in ChatGPT with New Sales Invoicing, Payroll, and Lending Features Key takeaways Intuit QuickBooks is introducing new, actionable sales invoicing, payroll, and lending intelligence in Claude and ChatGPT – moving beyond read-only access to your data. These features enable small business users to perform tasks like creating invoices, looking up payroll details, and accessing loan benchmarking through conversation. QuickBooks customers can continue to power their Claude and ChatGPT experiences with the right context to their data and their business, and take action to make informed financial decisions with confidence. Running a small business has always meant wearing every hat: owner, accountant, HR department, and billing department, all before lunch. AI is changing that. Intuit has established multi-year partnerships with Anthropic and OpenAI to bring the future of trusted Financial Intelligence to you. Our goal is to make Intuit’s expert platform and deep financial expertise accessible wherever you already work. With our connector in Claude and plugin in ChatGPT , we’re moving beyond simple answers to actionable results for your business, all powered by the same accuracy, security, and financial expertise you already trust in QuickBooks. This extends our core promise to meet you at more of the places you already work, bringing your financial data and workflows directly into the AI tools that you already use. According to Intuit’s 2026 AI Impact Report , 78% of US businesses say AI has improved their productivity, and 43% say it has increased their revenue. The businesses seeing those results are the ones putting AI to work inside real workflows, not just asking it generic questions. Today, our QuickBooks experience gets significantly more powerful and expands what small businesses can do inside Claude and ChatGPT with major new capabilities: sales, payroll, and capital lending intelligence, that builds upon the QuickBooks connector in Claude for Small Business and the QuickBooks plugin in ChatGPT . These new features, such as a full sales quote-to-cash workflow, deeper payroll query tools, and QuickBooks Capital’s peer loan benchmarking, mean that more of the work that you do running a business can continue to happen through conversation. This is moving beyond read-only access to your data. It’s your business, fully actionable. Not connected yet? Here’s how. Connect QuickBooks to Claude Adding QuickBooks to your Claude account takes three steps: Step 1: Open your Claude.ai account and navigate to the Customize tab in the left sidebar. Step 2: Click Connectors, search for “QuickBooks,” and select the connector from the results. Step 3: Click Connect and start asking questions about your business. Connect QuickBooks to ChatGPT Step 1: In ChatGPT , find Plugins in the left sidebar. Search for “Intuit QuickBooks” and click Connect Intuit QuickBooks. Step 2: Sign in to your QuickBooks account or create one. You’ll be returned to ChatGPT after signing in. Step 3: From the Intuit QuickBooks plugin, click Start chat and put your business finances to work. What’s new: three major features Sales: The full quote-to-cash loop, through conversation From finding a customer to sending an invoice and payment links*, your sales workflow now runs through QuickBooks in Claude and ChatGPT. What you can do: Invoicing, end-to-end: Create, update, send, and delete invoices; pull invoices with filters; duplicate an existing invoice as a starting point. Recurring invoices: Set up, update, pause/resume, and manage invoices that bill on a schedule. Sending invoice reminders: Send reminders on overdue invoices. Estimates, end-to-end: Create, update, send, and delete estimates; duplicate to reuse; bulk-fetch for review. Payment links: Generate a link for collection; filter and list existing links; email directly to customers.* Customer management: Create new customers with full contact details; search your list before invoicing. Products & services: Add new items to your catalog; search by description before building a line item. Transaction documents: Download any invoice or estimate as a PDF, ready for sharing or archiving. These are complete done-for-you experiences. You can prompt, ‘create an invoice for Acme Corporation for last week’s consulting work,’ review and send it—all without leaving your conversation. Payroll: Answers to your most common questions, without opening a report New payroll tools are now available to QuickBooks customers in Claude and ChatGPT—new payroll Q&A tools that go beyond the payroll-planning support already available. What you can ask: “Who’s on payroll?” — employee lookup by name, full roster, individual details “How much did we pay an employee last week?” — payslip history with filters by employee, ID, and date range “What benefits do we offer?” — company-wide deductions, benefits, and pay types “What are our time-off policies?” — company accrual rules and time-off configurations “Am I ready to run payroll?” — company’s payroll readiness status No more opening a report to answer a basic question. Your payroll intelligence is right there in the conversation. Capital: Lending intelligence that only QuickBooks can provide QuickBooks capital’s peer loan benchmarking tool is now available in the QuickBooks connector in Claude and plugin in ChatGPT. It’s the first time QuickBooks Capital data has been queryable through an external AI platform. When you ask about lending options, you’ll see anonymized, aggregated data based on the top 10% of QuickBooks businesses like yours. This is real data that helps you evaluate an offer, compare rates, and make a more confident financing decision. Questions you can now ask: “What are businesses like mine borrowing through QuickBooks Capital, and at what rates?” “Is this APR normal for a company like mine?” “What loan amount do similar businesses typically get approved for?” “When is my next term loan payment due?” This is lending intelligence only QuickBooks is uniquely positioned to provide, built on real small business data and surfaced in plain language exactly when you need it. This is what purpose-built AI for small business looks like AI is increasingly where people go first for financial decisions, and those decisions carry real consequences for cash flow, for teams, for livelihoods. That’s why it matters that the AI you’re using is grounded in real, current data from the system that actually runs your business. As a QuickBooks customer, you can continue to power your Claude and ChatGPT experiences with the right context to your data and your business, and also take action to make informed financial decisions with confidence. The benchmarks, patterns, and insights built into QuickBooks reflect your real-world financial behavior at scale, turned into practical guidance you can act on immediately via the QuickBooks connector in Claude and plugin in ChatGPT. And because QuickBooks is a native connector, it works alongside everything else you’ve plugged into Claude and ChatGPT: draft the proposal, turn it into an estimate, send the invoice, and follow up on payment from your customer, all in the same session where you run the rest of your day. This is what purpose-built AI for small business looks like. Your data, your control Trust is the foundation of everything we build and financial data remains yours. When you connect the QuickBooks connector in Claude or plugin in ChatGPT, we selectively apply your data to power trusted, accurate responses at your request. Your data stays within our Intuit systems and is never used to train foundation models. You retain full control over your business, and every action remains reviewable and human-verified. What’s coming next This is only the beginning. Upcoming features include: Payroll done-for-you experiences and actions — run payroll, manage compensation changes and import payroll data from other AI platforms and tools Personalized lending offers — surface your own Term Loan or line-of-credit options, not just peer benchmarks Creditworthiness intelligence — deeper insight into the factors that can affect your eligibility for financing With the QuickBooks connector in Claude and plugin in ChatGPT — now expanded with sales, payroll, and capital capabilities — you can move beyond simple answers to actionable results for your business, right inside your conversation. For more details on how these features are transforming your small business operations, visit our QuickBooks AI resource hub and our latest product update . Already connected? These new capabilities are available now — no extra setup required. New to QuickBooks on Claude or ChatGPT? Connect at claude.ai or find the Intuit QuickBooks plugin in ChatGPT to get started today. Money movement services are provided by Intuit Payments Inc., licensed as a Money Transmitter by the New York State Department of Financial Services. For details about our money transmission licenses, or for Texas customers with complaints about our service, please visit https://www.intuit.com/legal/licenses/payment-licenses/ . * Certain features require QuickBooks Payments: QuickBooks Payments account subject to eligibility criteria, credit, and application approval. Subscription to QuickBooks Online required. Not available in U.S. territories or outside the U.S. QuickBooks Term Loan and QuickBooks Line of Credit loans are issued by WebBank. QuickBooks Capital is licensed as Intuit Financing Inc. (NMLS #1136148), a subsidiary of Intuit Inc. This information is intended to outline our general product direction, but represents no obligation and should not be relied on in making a purchasing decision. Additional terms, conditions and fees may apply with certain features and functionality. Eligibility criteria may apply. Product offers, features, and functionality are subject to change without notice. title: Leggett & Platt Announces Quarterly Dividend of $.05
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Leggett & Platt's business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: CARTHAGE, Mo. , July 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Leggett & Platt's Board of Directors declared a dividend of $.05 per share for the third quarter of 2026. The dividend will be paid on August 24, 2026 to shareholders of record on August 10, 2026. FOR MORE INFORMATION: Visit Leggett's website at www.leggett.com . COMPANY DESCRIPTION: Leggett & Platt (NYSE: LEG) is a diversified manufacturer that designs and produces a broad variety of engineered components and products that can be found in many homes and automobiles. The 143-year-old Company is a leading supplier of bedding components and solutions; automotive seat comfort and convenience systems; home and work furniture components; geo components; flooring underlayment; and hydraulic cylinders for material handling and heavy construction applications. title: What Is CRM Integration: A 2026 Guide for Agencies
summary: Discover what is CRM integration and how it streamlines your agency workflows. This 2026 guide covers benefits, use cases, and a deployment checklist.
body_text: CRM integration is the process of connecting a CRM with other business tools so customer data moves between sales, marketing, and service systems without manual re-entry. In a mid-sized agency, that usually means the lead is in the CRM, the calendar lives elsewhere, hours sit in a separate tracker, and the COO is still waiting on a Monday report that won't land until Wednesday. The gap between those tools is where the pain sits. Teams spend time copying data, fixing mismatches, and arguing over which number is right, while the CRM slowly turns from a helpful record into a source of doubt. The simple answer and why it matters A common agency day looks like this. A new lead lands in the CRM, the account manager books time in Google Calendar, the project lead logs hours in another system, and finance wants a clean view of utilization before the weekly ops meeting. By the time everyone has checked their own tool, the report is already stale. That is why CRM integration matters. It connects the CRM to the rest of the stack so customer data moves between systems without manual re-entry, and the next team sees the update where it works from. carBoost CRM features is a useful example of how CRM data can be tied to broader operational workflows, which is the central purpose here. This is not a niche IT task anymore. 91% of companies with 10 or more employees use CRM software , and 74% of businesses in the United States have implemented a CRM system to manage customer interactions, according to the CRM statistics gathered by CRM.org . That scale matters because a CRM has moved from a contact database to the operating layer for customer-facing work. Practical rule: if the CRM is already where sales, service, or delivery teams look first, integration is part of the operating model. The money side is hard to ignore too. Nucleus Research-based reporting puts the average return at $8.71 for every $1 spent on CRM software, and other industry summaries say CRM users are 86% more likely to exceed sales goals than non-users, both cited in the CRM statistics round-up . For agencies, that promise only shows up when the CRM reflects the work being done. A cleaner way to see it is this. Integration is a discipline for keeping records trustworthy as work moves across tools. Sales can qualify a lead, project teams can update delivery status, billing can see what changed, and the CRM stays useful because the same customer story is showing up in each place. That is also why tools such as carBoost CRM features matter, because they show how CRM data stops being isolated and starts supporting the rest of the operation. That is the blunt version. If utilization is fuzzy, billing is delayed, and reporting takes a human chain of handoffs, the issue is often not the CRM itself. It is that the CRM is cut off from the tools where the work really happens. How CRM integration actually works At a basic level, each app keeps its own database, and the integration layer is the translator between them. When a contact is added in one tool, a trigger fires, the data gets mapped field by field, and the record lands in the CRM or another connected system. That same flow can then kick off updates in downstream tools. The moving parts you need to name The clean way to think about it is simple. One system owns the record, one layer moves the data, and the rest of the stack reacts to the change. Salesforce's integration guidance describes this as a multi-system data synchronization problem , not just a UI connection, because each app may live in cloud, legacy, or on-prem environments and the integration has to handle authentication, field mapping, rate limits, and system-of-record ownership. The terms matter because they shape the setup. System of record means the tool that owns the truth for a specific object, like a contact or a deal. Sync direction tells you whether data moves one way or both ways. Cadence tells you whether updates happen in real time with webhooks or on a schedule with batches. TimeTackle's API and data integration overview fits this model well because the point is not just moving records, it is deciding how and when those records move. Why “connected” is not the same as “reliable” A lot of teams stop at the word connected and assume the work is done. It isn't. If field ownership is unclear, you get duplicate records, stale values, and manual workarounds, which is exactly the kind of mess Salesforce warns about in its CRM integration guidance. If the mapping is solid and the ownership rules are clear, the sync can run in real time or on a schedule without people babysitting it. A calendar analogy works here. You would not let two calendars be the source of truth for one account meeting, so don't let two systems fight over the same customer field. The practical takeaway is plain. The hard part is not making apps talk. The hard part is making sure they say the same thing, at the right time, with the right owner attached to every field. Common integration patterns and how to choose one Mid-sized agencies usually end up with four patterns. Some are quick and narrow, some are flexible but heavier, and one or two will fit your stack better than the rest. The mistake is treating them like equal choices when they really aren't. The four patterns side by side Pattern Setup time Flexibility Maintenance burden Native connectors Low Low to medium Low iPaaS middleware Medium to high High Medium Custom API integrations High Very high High Reverse ETL Medium Medium to high Medium Native connectors are the built-in links inside the CRM or the app itself. They work well for obvious connections like email, calendar, and support tools, and they usually keep the setup simple. iPaaS tools like Workato or Tray sit in the middle and give you more control when one workflow crosses several systems. Custom APIs give you the most control, but they also ask the most from your engineering or ops team. Reverse ETL pushes warehouse data back into the CRM, which is useful when analytics is driving the action. For a 50 to 200 person agency , I'd start with native connectors for the obvious tools, then move to iPaaS only when a workflow spans more than three systems. That gives you a default path instead of a vague “it depends” answer. If your sales inbox, calendar, and service desk can sync through built-in tools, use them first. A practical example from agency work TimeTackle's project-management integration material shows the shape of a native-plus-API pattern that works well for operational teams. A calendar-to-time-tracking flow can pull activity from Google Calendar or Outlook, then push it into reporting without forcing the team into a separate manual logging habit. TimeTackle's project management integrations is worth a look if your current setup is a patchwork of calendar data, time tracking, and CRM context. The trade-off is clear. Native connectors are easier to live with, but they can be limited. Custom builds are powerful, but someone has to own them when the vendor changes a field, a permission, or an API rule. Benefits and ROI for mid-sized agencies The value of CRM integration shows up in the work ops leaders already struggle to keep aligned. Faster reporting, cleaner billing, better utilization visibility, and less time spent reconciling the same data in three tools. The return comes from removing the manual work around the connection, not from the connection itself. What gets better in practice When CRM data flows cleanly into the rest of the stack, reporting cycles stop depending on repeated export work. Finance gets a more consistent picture of what was sold, what was delivered, and what still needs a billing check. Project leads also get a clearer view of who is busy, who is underused, and where time is getting lost. Every unbilled hour cuts into margin. If the CRM and the rest of the system agree on client, project, and activity data, teams stop spending time checking who entered what and when. That is the point where integration starts paying back in daily operations, not just in dashboards that look tidy on a screen. A mid-sized agency usually sees the payoff in small but repeated wins. Reconciliation takes less time because the same client and project records appear the same way in sales, delivery, and finance tools. Managers spend less time fixing mismatched fields. Account teams spend less time answering basic questions about which system is right. Each of those savings is modest on its own, but together they reduce the drag that slows reporting, billing, and resourcing. But I would not oversell it. Integration will not fix a broken sales process, and it will not clean up bad data by magic. If field names are messy or people do not trust the numbers, the connection just moves the mess faster. ROI comes from data trust . Once people believe the CRM matches the work, they stop building shadow reports and side spreadsheets, which is where a lot of the hidden waste lives. Technical and security considerations to plan for A good integration plan is mostly a checklist of decisions. Who authenticates, what gets synced, which system owns each field, and how often the data moves. If those choices are fuzzy, the rollout becomes a support problem later. The decisions that matter before launch Authentication comes first. Some tools use OAuth , which is usually better when you want scoped access and easier revocation, while others still depend on API keys for simpler service-to-service links. Rate limits come next, because they shape how often you can sync without getting blocked or delayed. If the API is strict, a real-time dream may need to become a scheduled batch. Encryption should be a default, not a debate. Data should stay protected in transit and at rest , and access should be limited to the people and services that need it. Audit logs matter too, because when a record changes, you want to know what changed it and which system did it. For B2B SaaS agencies that integrate customer CRMs, the multi-tenant issue is real. Every customer can bring different custom fields, different API quotas, and different business rules, so the integration layer has to isolate tenant state instead of assuming one shared setup for everyone. That is why staged rollout matters. Truto's 2026 architecture guidance says to start in staging with realistic test data, then enable only a small subset of records in production while watching logs for missing required fields and duplicates. Operational rule: if a field, an event, or a permission is not explicitly owned by someone, it will become a problem within a quarter. TimeTackle's product pages say the platform is SOC 2 Type II certified and uses enterprise-grade encryption, which is the kind of baseline you want from a tool that sits near customer and calendar data. That doesn't remove the need for your own access rules, but it does lower the risk of starting from a weak security posture. The short version is this. Treat security as part of the design, not a review step at the end. Once the sync runs, every missing ownership rule turns into a cleanup task. Four use cases that show integration in action The easiest way to judge CRM integration is to look at the manual work it removes. If a workflow still depends on one person copying the same details from one screen to another, the integration is not finished. Marketing to sales handoff A form fill should land in the CRM with attribution attached and duplicates handled before sales ever sees it. Without that, two reps may chase the same lead, or the account may be split across multiple records. With the integration in place, the handoff is simple, and the rep starts with the right context instead of a blank slate. Support to customer success When support tickets update the account record, customer success can spot trouble sooner. Before integration, a ticket might sit in a support tool while the health score stays untouched in the CRM. Afterward, the score reflects the account's actual state, which means the team doesn't wait for a weekly review to notice a problem. Calendar to utilization Calendar data is one of the cleanest agency signals because the work already happened there. Meetings tagged in Google or Outlook can feed a time-tracking system like TimeTackle, so utilization reports stop depending on manual timesheet entry. TimeTackle's HubSpot calendar integration guide shows how this kind of bridge can connect calendar activity back to CRM work without turning every employee into a data clerk. Ecommerce to CRM If you work with clients that sell online, order history and support tickets should sit on the same account view. That lets customer success see churn risk without digging through separate tools. It also keeps the sales team from missing the fact that a customer's recent order or open issue changes the conversation. The pattern is consistent. Integration earns its keep when it removes a recurring task that a real person hates doing. If nobody misses the old manual step, the workflow probably wasn't painful enough to justify the build. Your rollout checklist and what to watch after go-live The safest rollout is boring. Start in staging with realistic test data, check the field mapping, then turn on only a small slice of records in production while someone watches the logs. If the first batch lands cleanly, expand from there. The rollout order I'd use Pick one workflow. Start with the process that creates the most manual pain, not the one that sounds the most impressive. Map the fields. Define exactly which source field lands where, and decide who owns the truth for each object. Choose the pattern. Use a native connector, iPaaS, custom API, or reverse ETL based on the scope, not habit. Ship a small version. Turn it on for a narrow set of records first, then widen it after you've watched the logs. The biggest post-launch problems are predictable. Inconsistent field mapping creates mismatched records, so the fix is a stricter field map and a named owner. Duplicate records need dedupe rules before the sync expands. API limits force you to slow the cadence or batch the updates. Delayed sync usually means the schedule is too aggressive or the event logic is broken. Two more problems show up once teams start trusting the data. Workflow mismatches happen when one department expects a field to behave differently than another, so the answer is to document the rule and train people on it. Weak reporting and scalability issues usually mean the integration works technically but doesn't hold up under real use, so you need review cycles and clear ownership after launch. The point is simple. CRM integration is not a one-time project, it is an ongoing governance job. The risk is that everyone trusts the data for a month, then stops trusting it six months later because no one owns the cleanup. Start with one workflow, map the fields, choose the pattern, and ship it. If you want a tool built around calendar-driven time capture and operational reporting, take a look at TimeTackle and compare it against the way your team already works. title: Year-End Financial Checklist for Contractors 2025
summary: If you've got uncashed checks in your truck, receipts in your glovebox, and your accountant's already texting about year-end while your QuickBooks hasn't been reconciled since September, this checklist is for you. This year-end financial guide helps construction contractors wrap up 2025 efficiently by reconciling accounts and collecting outstanding invoices, maximizing tax deductions before December 31st with Section 179 ($1.25M limit) and 40% bonus depreciation, preparing 1099s for the January 31st, 2026 deadline, reviewing banking infrastructure costs, and planning 2026 cash flow with clear financial goals. The guide includes specific deadlines and an action plan so you can close out the year strong without spending your entire holiday season buried in paperwork.
body_text: It's December, and Your Books Are a Mess You just wrapped a big project. The client's happy, the work looks great, but you've got three uncashed checks sitting in your truck, a pile of receipts in your glovebox, and you're pretty sure you forgot to invoice someone back in October. Your accountant's already texting about tax documents, and you haven't reconciled your QuickBooks since... September? Sound familiar? Year-end doesn't have to be chaos. This checklist will help you wrap up 2025 efficiently, find money you didn't know was sitting there, and enter 2026 with clean books and predictable cash flow - without spending your entire holiday season buried in paperwork. 1. Reconcile All Accounts and Outstanding Invoices Review Outstanding Receivables Go through every unpaid invoice and categorize them: Collectible within 30 days - Follow up immediately with payment reminders Aged 30-60 days - Escalate with phone calls and payment plans Aged 60+ days - Consider collection strategies or write-offs for tax purposes Many contractors discover thousands of dollars in forgotten invoices during year-end reviews. Pro tip: If you're still waiting for checks, you're adding 10-12 days to every payment cycle. Switch to digital invoicing with payment links so clients can pay instantly, and you can close out receivables before December 31st. Reconcile Bank Statements and Accounts Payable Match every transaction in your bank account to your accounting records ‍ If you're using QuickBooks but manually entering transactions, this process can take days. Automated QuickBooks integration syncs payments and expenses in real-time, eliminating reconciliation headaches. Don't forget what you owe . List all outstanding vendor and subcontractor payments, verify payment terms, and confirm 1099 information is accurate. With streamlined vendor payment tools , you can schedule payments efficiently without manual check-writing. 2. Maximize Tax Deductions Before December 31st Year-end is your last chance to reduce your 2025 tax liability. Accelerate Deductible Expenses If you're planning major purchases for early 2026, consider buying them in December instead: Equipment and tools - Section 179 allows you to deduct the full cost of qualifying equipment (up to $1,250,000 for 2025) Vehicle purchases - Trucks and work vehicles may qualify for immediate expensing Software, supplies, and professional services - Prepay for items you'll use in 2026 Important: You must purchase AND place the item in service by December 31st to qualify for 2025 deductions. Consider Bonus Depreciation Bonus depreciation is phasing out: 2025: 40% bonus depreciation available 2026: Drops to 20% 2027: Drops to 0% If you're planning equipment purchases, doing them in 2025 gives you a higher first-year deduction. The window is closing. Review Retirement Contributions Contractors can make significant tax-deductible retirement contributions: Solo 401(k) - Up to $70,000 for 2025 ($77,500 if 50+) SEP IRA - Up to 25% of compensation, maximum $70,000 Simple IRA - Up to $16,500 ($20,000 if 50+) Consult your accountant about which option works best and the specific deadlines (some plans allow contributions into early 2026 for the 2025 tax year). Digital receipt capture through business card services can automatically categorize and store receipts, making tax time significantly easier. Disclaimer: Tax laws are complex and change frequently. Always consult with a qualified accountant or tax professional for personalized advice specific to your business situation. 3. Prepare for 1099 Filing Requirements If you paid any subcontractors or vendors $600 or more during 2025, you're required to file 1099-NEC forms by January 31st, 2026. Create Your 1099 List Now Don't wait until January: List every subcontractor and vendor you paid $600+ in 2025 Verify you have W-9 forms on file for each (legal name, address, TIN/EIN) Calculate total payments made to each throughout the year Flag any missing information and collect it before year-end Common 1099 Mistakes to Avoid Missing W-9 forms - you can't file without the vendor's tax ID number Incorrect legal names - use the exact name from the W-9, not DBA names Wrong form type - most contractors need 1099-NEC, not 1099-MISC Late filing - January 31st deadline is firm; late filing incurs penalties Payment Method Tip Payments made via credit card or payment processor are reported by the processor, not by you. If you paid a subcontractor via business check, you file a 1099. If you paid via credit card, the card processor files it. This is one reason many contractors are switching to card-based vendor payments. 4. Review Your Banking Infrastructure Year-end is the perfect time to evaluate whether your banking setup is helping or hurting your business. Calculate What Your Current Banking Costs You Most contractors don't realize the true cost: Hours spent on bank trips and waiting for checks to clear (3-5 days) Monthly account fees, wire transfer fees, check ordering costs Payment processing fees that eat into margins Limited FDIC coverage (only $250K standard) Opportunity cost of delayed payments Many contractors discover they're losing $10,000-$30,000+ annually to inefficient banking processes. What Modern Construction Banking Should Include As you plan for 2026, your banking infrastructure should provide: Instant invoice payment options (ACH, card, wire) with payment links Automatic QuickBooks sync when payments arrive Free ACH transfers to vendors and digital bill pay Extended FDIC coverage beyond $250K (look for $3M+) Real-time financial visibility across all projects Mobile access for jobsite payments If your current banking setup doesn't check these boxes, you're starting 2026 with the same inefficiencies that slowed you down in 2025. Explore banking built specifically for construction . 5. Plan Your 2026 Cash Flow and Goals Project Your Q1 Cash Needs Construction often slows in winter, but your expenses don't. Estimate your fixed costs for January-March, list projects starting in Q1, and identify potential cash flow crunches before they happen. If you have strong cash flow in December, consider setting aside 3-6 months of operating expenses as an emergency fund. Set Clear Financial Targets for 2026 Define specific, measurable goals: Revenue target and profit margin percentage Project volume and average project size Days sales outstanding (DSO) target Review Your Pricing Use year-end financial data to inform pricing decisions. Calculate your true cost per project type, identify which services are most profitable, and adjust pricing to account for 2026 cost increases (labor, materials, insurance). 6. Take Action Before December 31st Year-end financial planning isn't something you can do in January. Many of these strategies only work if you take action now. Your Year-End Action Plan: This Week: Pull your outstanding receivables report and start collection calls List all subcontractors who need 1099s and verify you have their W-9s Schedule a meeting with your accountant to discuss tax strategies Before December 15th: Make any equipment purchases you want to deduct in 2025 Reconcile all bank and credit card accounts Review and maximize retirement contributions Before December 31st: Collect as many outstanding invoices as possible Pay any expenses you want to deduct this year Finalize your 1099 contractor list Set up your 2026 financial tracking systems Early January 2026: File 1099s by January 31st deadline Meet with accountant to finalize tax returns Review year-end reports and set 2026 goals Enter 2026 With Confidence The difference between contractors who grow consistently and those who struggle often comes down to financial systems and planning. You can't control material costs or weather delays - but you can control how efficiently your money moves. Truss delivers enterprise-grade banking infrastructure built exclusively for construction businesses . We combine deposit accounts with up to $3M FDIC coverage, instant payment processing, seamless QuickBooks integration, and vendor payment tools in one simple platform - so you can close out 2025 strong and enter 2026 with the financial infrastructure to support your growth. Ready to streamline your construction banking? title: Dreamforce 2026: Your complete attendee travel guide
summary: Plan your Dreamforce 2026 trip with hotel pricing, San Francisco budget tips, and networking advice. Learn when to book to beat conference-week premium.
body_text: Dreamforce draws more than 40,000 people to San Francisco every September at the Moscone Center for Salesforce's ecosystem, its partners, and anyone selling to, buying from, or competing with them. The sessions are valuable. The hallway conversations are even more valuable. And the dinner you have with a prospect during the conference might be the most valuable moment of the entire week. This guide covers the logistics that make the conference worth attending: how to book smart, budget accurately, build a session strategy that won't leave you burned out by day two, and follow up in a way that turns conversations into pipeline. Why Dreamforce 2026 is worth the trip Dreamforce 2026 runs September 15 through 17 at Moscone Center (North, South, and West halls) in San Francisco. This year's theme is “Agentic Enterprise,” and Marc Benioff will deliver the opening keynote alongside speakers including Sterling K. Brown, Swan Sit, Tony Robbins, Sheryl Lee Ralph, Matthew McConaughey, and Renée Richardson Gosline. The scale is staggering: 1,600+ sessions, 150+ hands-on trainings, and an attendee count that regularly tops 40,000. A full conference pass costs $2,299, though early-bird pricing drops to $1,499 if you register before July 16, and groups of five or more pay $999 per pass. Every pass includes all keynotes, breakout sessions, theater sessions, workshops, roundtables, the Welcome Reception, Dreamfest, and daily refreshments plus lunch. But the real value isn't on the main stage. It's in the hallway track, the partner receptions, and the community meetups. It's also in the dinners that happen after the sessions end, as Dreamforce week extends well beyond the boundaries of the convention center: dev happy hours, exec dinners, and Dreamfest (a concert event included with every pass) fill the evenings. Who attends The crowd is broad; it includes Salesforce admins, developers, CTOs, sales leaders, consultants, startup founders, and partner ecosystem executives. If your company uses Salesforce or sells to companies that do, a significant share of your target market walks Moscone's halls for three days straight. The density of decision-makers per square foot is hard to replicate at any other single event. For anyone considering a pre-event deep dive, the Trailblazer Bootcamp runs September 12 through 14. It's three additional days of hands-on training before the main conference begins. Book your flights and a hotel near Moscone Center early Conference-week hotel prices near Moscone don't behave like regular San Francisco rates. An anonymized analysis of 1,337 hotel bookings near Moscone Center during Dreamforce 2025 week shows a median nightly rate of $569 — an 87% premium over a normal September week's median rate of $305. The booking window matters more than most travelers realize. Those who booked two or more months before check-in paid a median of $483 per night. Those who waited until the last minute paid $587. Yet 36.4% of travelers still booked within two weeks of the conference, and 22.8% booked within seven days. The sweet spot is clear. Book early or pay the procrastination tax. The official hotel block deadline is August 21, 2026. Compare the block rate against open-market pricing before committing. In some years, early open-market rates undercut the block; in others, the block guarantees availability when everything else sells out. Check both. Where to stay Three hotel zones work for Dreamforce, each with a different trade-off: SoMa (5-minute walk to Moscone). Marriott Marquis, InterContinental, Hyatt Regency, The Clancy. Highest convenience, highest price. If walkability is non-negotiable, this is your zone. Union Square (10 to 12 minutes on foot). Better restaurant selection, BART and Muni access at Powell Station. One caveat: The east side of Union Square borders the Tenderloin, so check your hotel's specific block before booking, especially if you'll be walking back late. Embarcadero (15-minute commute). Best waterfront views and waterfront dining along the bay. Ideal if you're comfortable with a short rideshare or Muni ride and want a quieter neighborhood for the evenings. The Ferry Building has strong breakfast and coffee options in this zone. Simplify travel bookings with Navan Edge Instead of toggling between booking sites for flights and hotels, Navan Edge gives you a single agentic AI-powered chat, backed by an elite human concierge team, to book flights, hotels, and restaurants based on your preferences and real-time inventory. For Dreamforce, that means telling it your dates, loyalty programs, and hotel amenities that matter for business travel, and getting options filtered to what actually fits, without opening a dozen tabs. Set a realistic San Francisco budget before you go San Francisco's GSA per diem rate for September 2026 is $272 for lodging and $92 for meals and incidental expenses (M&IE), totaling $364 per day. The M&IE breaks down to $23 for breakfast, $26 for lunch, $38 for dinner, and $5 for incidentals. On your first and last travel days, M&IE drops to $69 (75% of the full rate). Rates are subject to change; verify current figures at GSA.gov. Now compare that $272 lodging allowance to what Dreamforce attendees actually pay. The median nightly rate near Moscone during Dreamforce 2025 week was $569 — a $297-per-night gap between what the government considers reasonable and what the market charges during the conference. If your company reimburses at the GSA rate, you're structurally underfunded unless you book early (2+ months out brought the median down to $483) or stay farther from Moscone. If you're self-funding, budget $500 to $600 per night for a walkable SoMa hotel, or $350 to $450 for Union Square or Embarcadero. For a 3-night stay (the most common), hotel costs alone run $1,450 to $1,800 near Moscone at conference-week rates. Add the $2,299 conference pass, flights, meals, and ground transportation, and a realistic all-in budget for Dreamforce is $4,500 to $6,000 per attendee. The early-bird pass ($1,499 through July 16) and early hotel booking ($483 median at 2+ months out) are the two biggest levers for reducing that number. Groups of five or more get an even steeper conference discount at $999 per pass, which is worth coordinating if multiple team members are attending. Hidden costs to plan for Rideshare surge pricing. Conference week pushes Uber and Lyft prices up across SoMa, especially during morning arrivals and evening event rushes. Premium dinners. Client dinners near Moscone run $75 to $200+ per person at the restaurants worth visiting. After-hours events. Some partner receptions and exec dinners are ticketed separately from the conference pass. Conference-provided meals. Your pass includes daily refreshments and lunch, which offsets the M&IE deduction. Factor that savings into your daily budget. Booking through Navan Edge earns you not only loyalty points, credit card rewards, but also 5% back in Amazon Gift Cards on eligible hotel stays, stacking three reward layers on a single booking. Build your agenda before you land Since Dreamforce features 1,600+ sessions and 150+ hands-on trainings, the temptation may be to pack every minute with one of them. Resist it. Three to four sessions per day is the sustainable cap; beyond that, retention drops and fatigue compounds. Prioritize formats that only work in person. Workshops, roundtables, and hands-on training require physical presence. Keynotes and theater sessions are often available on replay via Salesforce+ after the conference. Skip the replayable ones live and rather use that time for conversations that can only happen face-to-face. Pre-conference checklist Download the Dreamforce mobile app. Session schedules, venue maps, and real-time capacity updates live there. Build your agenda in the app before you land. Set OOO messages. Block your calendar for the conference dates and the travel day on either side. Confirm meetings. If you've scheduled coffees or 1:1s, reconfirm 48 hours before. No-shows spike at large conferences. Prepare your contact-sharing method. QR codes and NFC-based sharing (via Apple Wallet or LinkedIn) are faster than business cards. Whatever method you choose, add a note about the conversation topic within an hour of each exchange. The note is what makes the contact useful later. Build a target list of 10 to 15 people you want to meet. Send personalized outreach two weeks before the conference. Include something specific: Reference a session they're speaking at, a product they launched, or a mutual connection. Generic “let's connect at Dreamforce” messages get ignored. If you're bringing a team, assign coverage. Who attends which sessions? Who targets which contacts? Divide the conference so each person covers different ground, then merge insights at the end of each day. Three people attending the same keynote produces one takeaway — three people in three different rooms produces three. What to wear and what to pack for Dreamforce The dress code at Dreamforce is tech-casual: blazer over a tee, clean sneakers or loafers, no ties required. Adjust upward if you're in client-facing meetings or pitching investors; a sport coat and collared shirt still signals “I take this seriously” without overdressing for the crowd. September is San Francisco's warmest month, with average highs of 70 to 73 degrees Fahrenheit, lows of 56 to 57 degrees, and minimal rain. But SF's microclimates mean SoMa (near Moscone) runs warmer while western neighborhoods are cooler and foggier. Evening temperatures drop noticeably. Bring layers. Experienced-traveler packing list Two pairs of shoes. Bring broken-in walking shoes for the convention floor (expect 20,000+ steps per day) and a dinner-appropriate pair for evening events. 20,000mAh battery pack. Your phone is your conference app, your map, your contact-sharing tool, and your camera. It won't last three days on its own. Reusable water bottle. Moscone has refill stations. Hydration is the single easiest burnout prevention tool. Hand sanitizer and immune support. 40,000+ people in enclosed spaces means “conference crud” is a real risk. Zinc, vitamin C, and hand hygiene reduce your odds of getting sick. Earplugs or noise-canceling headphones. For sleeping and quiet breaks during the conference. Light jacket. For evening walks and air-conditioned session rooms. Chargers and adapters. International attendees: the U.S. uses Type A/B plugs. Arrival day: From the airport to Moscone Center SFO is the primary airport for Dreamforce. OAK (Oakland International) is a viable alternative, especially for domestic flights with lower fares. Mode From SFO From OAK Cost Notes BART ~30–40 minutes ~40–50 minutes $9–$10 Powell Station is nearest to Moscone Rideshare 30–60 minutes 40–60 minutes $30–$60 Expect surge pricing during conference week Waymo 30–60 minutes -- Variable Driverless option available in SF Rental car Not recommended Not recommended -- Expensive parking, traffic BART is the most reliable option. The ride from SFO to Powell Station takes about 35 minutes, costs under $10, and avoids conference-week traffic entirely. From Powell, Moscone is a 10-minute walk south on 4th Street. No surge pricing, no traffic variability, no small talk with a driver while you're trying to prep for your first meeting. For those arriving at OAK, BART takes slightly longer (40 to 50 minutes) but is equally straightforward. Waymo, the driverless car service, is available in San Francisco for a novel alternative, though availability during peak conference arrivals is unpredictable. When attendees actually arrive Anonymized flight data from Dreamforce 2025 week shows 5,920 flights carrying business travelers to SFO and OAK, with 25.2% originating internationally. The NYC metro area was the largest corridor with 907 flights, followed by Melbourne (279), Atlanta (277), Toronto (266), and Seattle (257). Most hotel check-ins happened on Monday, with Thursday being the most common checkout day. Most people arrive Sunday evening or Monday morning and departing Thursday. Arrive the night before. If your first session is Tuesday morning, fly in Monday evening. The cost of one extra hotel night is a fraction of the productivity you lose by arriving jet-lagged on day one. For cross-country or international arrivals, shift your sleep schedule 30 minutes per day in the days before departure, get daylight exposure immediately after landing, and skip the night-zero social events. A 25% international attendee base means a quarter of the room is fighting jet lag during Tuesday morning's opening keynote. Don't be one of the attendees who slept only four hours. If you need an early check-in, Navan Edge's 24/7 human travel experts can contact the hotel directly and negotiate the time. No phone trees, no hold music. During the conference The hallway track is the real conference. The sessions give you content. The conversations between sessions give you relationships, deals, and intelligence you can't get from a slide deck. Target three to five quality conversations per day. That's not “scan a badge and move on.” That's a genuine exchange where you learn something, share something, and walk away with a reason to follow up. The sessions give you knowledge, but the hallway makes way for new relationships and competitive intelligence that never make it into the keynote slides. Session strategy Attend in-person-only formats. Workshops, hands-on training, and roundtables where the interaction is the product. Skip sessions that will be on replay. Keynotes and theater sessions are typically available via Salesforce+ within days. Watch them at 1.5x speed from your hotel. Leave gaps. A packed schedule eliminates the serendipity that makes conferences valuable. Leave at least one open hour per half-day. Side events and after-hours Dreamforce's orbit includes partner receptions, community-led meetups, dev happy hours, exec dinners, and Dreamfest, which is included with every conference pass. To find them: Check the Dreamforce mobile app for official side events. Search the conference hashtag on LinkedIn and X (formerly Twitter). Ask exhibitors and sponsors directly; many host invite-only dinners that are announced at the booth. Watch your email the week before; partner invitations spike in the final 10 days. The Welcome Reception on opening night is worth attending. It's low-pressure, well-organized, and gives you a chance to get oriented before the sessions begin. Use it to scope out the venue layout, test your contact-sharing method on someone low-stakes, and identify the quiet corners you'll retreat to later in the week. Networking that turns Dreamforce into pipeline Networking at a 40,000-person conference without a plan is just socializing. The framework that works is simple: before, during, and after. Before Dreamforce Build a target list of 10 to 15 people. Use the attendee list (if published), speaker bios, and LinkedIn to identify who you want to meet. Send personalized outreach two weeks before the conference. Reference something specific: a session they're presenting, a product they launched, a shared connection. Schedule coffees and 1:1 meetings outside the main session blocks. During Dreamforce Lead with curiosity, not a pitch. Ask what they're working on, what sessions surprised them, what problems they're trying to solve. The goal is information exchange, not a sales call. Use a buddy system if you're attending with colleagues. Split up and work different rooms, different sessions, different dinners. Debrief each evening to share contacts and insights. Capture context immediately. After every meaningful conversation, take 30 seconds to write a note about who you spoke with, what you discussed, what they care about, and what you promised to send. A phone photo of their badge plus a voice memo works. The context is what makes the follow-up land. One underrated tactic: Schedule a 15-minute debrief with your team or travel companion at the end of each day. Share contacts, compare notes on sessions, and flag anyone the other person should meet tomorrow. Two people covering the same conference should produce twice the output, not twice the overlap. After Dreamforce The 48-hour follow-up window is the single most important networking rule. Within two days of the conference ending, send a personalized email referencing the specific conversation you had. Instead of saying “Great to meet you at Dreamforce!”, send something that proves you were paying attention. After 48 hours, the memory fades, the inbox fills, and your message becomes noise. The window is real. The follow-up doesn't need to be long; three sentences will do it. Remind them who you are, reference what you discussed, and propose a next step. “Great meeting you at the Data Cloud session. You mentioned struggling with attribution across Salesforce instances. Here's the case study I mentioned, and I'd love to set up a 20-minute call next week to walk through it.” Dinners, dining, and fueling yourself through three days Restaurant choices during Dreamforce aren't just about food — they're about context. A client dinner requires a different setting than a team celebration or a solo recharge meal. Near Moscone, by use case Client dinner: MKT at Four Seasons (upscale, walking distance from Moscone, impressive without being flashy) or Epic Steak (waterfront setting on the Embarcadero, strong for a relaxed power meal) Team celebration: Fogo de Chao (continuous service works well for groups, Brazilian steakhouse energy, accommodates large parties) Quieter one-on-one: KAIYO (Nikkei cuisine, more intimate atmosphere) or B Restaurant (rooftop location atop Moscone North with conference-week views) Navan Edge's destination intelligence surfaces restaurant recommendations matched to the type of restaurant you want. Tell it you're looking for a quiet place for a client dinner near your hotel, and it returns options filtered by cuisine, noise level, and availability, with booking handled in the same chat where you planned the rest of your business trip. Fuel strategy Conference food is designed for convenience, not performance. Protect your energy with a few habits: Eat a real breakfast outside the venue. Hotel restaurants or neighborhood cafes beat conference coffee and pastries. Take lunch outside the expo hall. The crowds, the noise, and the mediocre food aren't worth the time savings. Walk two blocks for something better. Bring snacks. Protein bars, trail mix, or dried fruit for the 3 p.m. session block when the convention center options are picked over. Hydrate constantly. Convention center air is dry, and you'll walk more than you expect. A refillable water bottle pays for itself in energy by midafternoon. If you're booking hotels through Navan Edge, each stay earns loyalty points, credit card rewards, and 5% back in Amazon Gift Cards on eligible hotel stays. Those rewards stack on every eligible hotel night during your Dreamforce trip, helping offset the conference-week premium. How to avoid conference burnout Three days at a 40,000-person conference will test your stamina. The attendees who leave Dreamforce with energy and results instead of exhaustion and regret follow a few deliberate patterns. Schedule less than you think you can handle. If you can attend six sessions, plan for four. The margins are where the best conversations happen. Break every three hours. Moscone has quiet areas on the upper levels. Your hotel room is a 5-minute walk if you're in SoMa. A 20-minute reset between session blocks makes the afternoon productive instead of performative. Sleep beats afterparties. If you have a 7 a.m. meeting or a session you flagged as must-attend, the 11 p.m. partner reception is not worth it. Choose deliberately. Hydrate and eat real food. A reusable water bottle and a real lunch are more effective than any productivity hack. Convention center air is dry, the walking is relentless (20,000+ steps per day on those floors), and skipping meals compounds fatigue fast. Conference crud prevention. Use hand sanitizer before and after every handshake. Take zinc and vitamin C starting two days before arrival. Bring earplugs for better hotel sleep. These aren't paranoid measures; they're practical tips in a crowd of 40,000. Personal safety in SoMa. San Francisco's SoMa neighborhood is generally safe during conference hours. After dark, stick to well-lit streets and avoid the 6th Street corridor. Rideshare back to your hotel if you're out late. Tips for departure day Most Dreamforce attendees check out on Thursday. The morning rush at SoMa hotels is predictable, and so is the rideshare surge to SFO. Pack the night before. Don't wait until the morning of — you might want the final morning for a last coffee, a quick meeting, or simply a calm start. Get a late checkout. Ask at check-in, not at checkout. Loyalty status (even mid-tier) often qualifies you for a 2 p.m. checkout. If you're using Navan Edge, its 24/7 human travel experts can negotiate late checkout directly with the hotel, freeing you to focus on your last conference meetings instead of haggling at the front desk. Use airport lounge access. SFO's terminals have multiple lounge options. An Amex Platinum card gets you into the Centurion Lounge in Terminal 3. Priority Pass opens up several other options. If you have a long wait, a lounge beats a gate seat after three days on a convention center floor. Buffer your travel time. Conference-week rideshare surge is real. Add 30 minutes to whatever Google Maps says. If you're taking BART, the trip is predictable, but factor in the walk from your hotel to Powell Station with luggage. Skip the hotel breakfast rush. Thursday morning at SoMa hotels is chaotic. Every Dreamforce attendee is checking out, eating breakfast, and calling rideshares at the same time. Grab coffee to go, get to the airport early, and eat at the lounge or gate. You'll save 30 minutes of lobby congestion. After Dreamforce 2026 The conference ended, but there's still work that can be done to ensure you get the most out of it. The 48-hour follow-up window This is the anchor of your post-conference week. Within 48 hours, send every follow-up email you committed to. Each one should reference the specific conversation: what you discussed, what they mentioned caring about, and what you're sending or proposing. After the 48-hour window, response rates drop sharply. Treat it as a deadline, not a suggestion. Share what you learned Post on LinkedIn within 24 hours. Tag the speakers who impressed you. Share one concrete takeaway, not a generic “great event.” The visibility compounds: Your contacts see the post, the speakers see the tag, and people who couldn't attend get value from your perspective. Schedule a team debrief within one week. Cover key themes, contacts made, follow-ups in progress, and competitive intelligence gathered. One person's Dreamforce trip should generate insights the whole team can use. Structure the debrief around three questions: What did we learn that changes our approach, who did we meet that we should engage, and what did competitors announce that we should respond to? File your expense report File while the details are fresh. Capture receipts for every client dinner, rideshare, and incidental before they blur together. If your company uses per diem reimbursement, document the dates and meals clearly to ensure you're reimbursed accurately. Gentle re-entry Don't fill your calendar the day after you return. Leave the first day back for processing: follow-ups, expense filing, and decompression. The worst post-conference move is diving into back-to-back meetings with a jet-lagged brain and an overflowing inbox. Block the Monday after Dreamforce as a “recovery and action” day. Use the morning for follow-up emails (the 48-hour window is closing). Use the afternoon for your team debrief. By Tuesday, you're back in normal operating mode with every contact captured, every expense filed, and every takeaway shared. Make your Dreamforce 2026 trip count The difference between a productive Dreamforce and a draining one isn't the sessions you attend or the parties you crash. It's the trip infrastructure underneath: the hotel that's walkable to Moscone, the budget you set before you booked, the networking targets you identified before you landed, and the follow-up emails you sent before the contact went cold. Plan the trip, and the conference delivers. Skip the planning and you'll spend the week reacting instead of operating. If you want the trip logistics handled for you, Navan Edge books flights, hotels, and restaurants in one conversation, remembers what matters to you, and has human travel experts available 24/7. It's free to use, and earns you air miles, loyalty points and credit card rewards, plus 5% back in Amazon Gift Cards with eligible hotel bookings. title: Marvell to Invest $250 Million in India, Expanding Bangalore Facility to Drive Next-generation AI Technology Development
summary: Investment Will Expand Technology, Talent and Infrastructure as Marvell Celebrates 20 Years of Engineering Innovation in India BANGALORE,…...
body_text: Marvell to Invest $250 Million in India, Expanding Bangalore Facility to Drive Next-generation AI Technology Development July 29, 2026 Investment Will Expand Technology, Talent and Infrastructure as Marvell Celebrates 20 Years of Engineering Innovation in India BANGALORE, India--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL), a leader in data infrastructure semiconductor solutions, today announced plans to invest $250 million in India over the next three years to expand its capabilities across technology, talent and infrastructure. The announcement coincides with a milestone event celebrating 20 years of innovation in India, highlighting the company’s contributions to global technology development, its continued investment in the region and its commitment to advancing India’s semiconductor ecosystem and engineering talent. As part of this investment, Marvell plans to double its headcount over the next three years and is unveiling a new wing at its Bangalore office while expanding its presence in Hyderabad. The expanded footprint will strengthen the company’s global innovation network, supporting the design and development of advanced semiconductor solutions for AI, cloud and data infrastructure applications. “India has become a strategic hub of engineering excellence for Marvell, playing a critical role in advancing the infrastructure technologies that power the world’s leading hyperscalers and cloud providers,” said Navin Bishnoi, vice president and India country manager, at Marvell. “As we celebrate 20 years in India, we remain committed to expanding R&D investments, strengthening the country’s semiconductor ecosystem and developing the next generation of technology talent. We are grateful to our customers, partners, government collaborators, academic institutions and especially our exceptional team, whose innovation, expertise and dedication have been instrumental to the growth and success of Marvell in India.” Advancing Semiconductor Innovation Marvell established operations in Bangalore in 2006 and has since grown India into the company’s second-largest R&D organization worldwide. Teams across Bangalore, Pune and Hyderabad have developed deep expertise in advanced process technologies (2nm and beyond), high-speed analog IP, subsystem design, software/firmware development and end-to-end silicon development. Today, Marvell India contributes across numerous technology platforms, with its employees holding multiple patents and is playing a leading role in applying advanced AI tools to accelerate engineering productivity and innovation. Beyond technology development, Marvell continues to invest in the long-term growth of India’s semiconductor ecosystem through collaboration with universities, startups, industry associations, and government organizations. Marvell collaborates with leading universities to support internship programs, faculty development initiatives, joint research projects, and curriculum development designed to better prepare students for careers in advanced technology fields. Marvell also works with emerging startups through mentorship and strategic collaborations in areas aligned with company technology and product portfolios. In addition, Marvell actively engages with industry associations and government bodies to foster greater collaboration across the ecosystem and support the continued growth of India’s semiconductor industry. Marvell Scholarship Program During the event, Marvell underscored its commitment to developing future engineering talent through its Marvell Scholarship for Technical and Engineering Merit (MSTEM) program, an initiative designed to help cultivate the next generation of AI and semiconductor innovators through financial support, hands-on industry experience, and exposure to real-world technology development. Launched earlier this year, the MSTEM program supports students pursuing degrees in electronics, electrical engineering, and computer science. The program attracted more than 7,000 applicants from leading universities across India, with 100 outstanding students selected to receive scholarships. By combining financial assistance with practical industry engagement, the program aims to strengthen India’s technology talent pipeline and prepare students for careers at the forefront of semiconductor and AI innovation. About Marvell To deliver the data infrastructure technology that connects the world, we’re building solutions on the most powerful foundation: our partnerships with our customers. Trusted by the world’s leading technology companies for over 30 years, we move, store, process and secure the world’s data with semiconductor solutions designed for our customers’ current needs and future ambitions. Through a process of deep collaboration and transparency, we’re ultimately changing the way tomorrow’s enterprise, cloud and carrier architectures transform—for the better. title: Tractian Raises $120M to Eliminate Industrial Downtime Worldwide
summary: Tractian, a leader in Manufacturing AI, secured a $120M Series C led by Sapphire Ventures, to expand its reach as the Industrial Copilot.
body_text: Led by Sapphire Ventures, the round will enable Tractian to drive innovation in Manufacturing AI and expand its reach as the trusted Industrial Copilot. ATLANTA, December 5, 2024 - Tractian, a leader in Manufacturing AI, secured $120M in Series C funding led by Sapphire Ventures, with participation from General Catalyst, Next47, and NGP Capital. This latest investment solidifies the Atlanta-based company as a key player in the industrial maintenance space. This funding will accelerate Tractian’s mission to optimize machine performance and ensure unprecedented uptime. As the Industrial Copilot, Tractian stands out by providing integrated hardware and software solutions for industrial asset monitoring, physical operations, and maintenance management, helping companies ensure zero downtime and improve technicians' productivity. Tractian addresses an estimated 5% of global industrial GDP. For every $1,000 produced by the world’s factories, $50 is generated in environments that rely on Tractian solutions. “We see Tractian as a transformative force in the industrial sector, addressing one of the most expensive challenges facing manufacturers today-unplanned downtime-with an AI solution that not only predicts issues, but drives operational ROI,” says Anders Ranum, Partner at Sapphire Ventures. “We’re thrilled to back Igor and the Tractian team, whose commitment to solving this problem stems from Igor’s firsthand experience growing up with a father who worked on a factory floor. We believe this passion makes them well suited to redefine industrial efficiency as we know it.” Tractian has also earned it a spot as the only manufacturing-focused company on the Forbes AI 50 list , which highlights the most promising artificial intelligence companies globally. The Industrial Copilot for Zero Downtime Eliminating Industrial Downtime and Closing a Massive Skills Gap Industrial maintenance is facing a growing crisis, with unplanned downtime now costing the world’s 500 largest companies 11% of their annual revenues-equivalent to $1.4 trillion (1). Recovery times have worsened dramatically, rising from an average of 49 minutes five years ago to 81 minutes today. This surge is fueled by systemic challenges: COVID has left critical skills gaps, while shifting global supply chains, compounding delays. Adding to the strain, modern equipment breakdowns have become harder to detect and repair. “With an aging workforce and fewer younger workers entering the field, the gap between human expertise and machine understanding widens. This loss of analog, hands-on knowledge has left industrial operations struggling to maintain efficiency.” says Igor Marinelli, Tractian CEO and co-founder. “There is growing momentum for the reshoring of manufacturing in the U.S., as companies seek to reduce dependencies and build more resilient supply chains.” Tractian streamlines maintenance and reliability into a cost-efficient, strategic advantage. Addressing downtime's root causes, Tractian closes the human-to-machine knowledge gap and delivers tailored insights, by combining proprietary models and LLM to cross-examine machine utilization, OEM specifications, and user-specific operational demands. Tractian continues to drive innovation with a team of 200+ engineers dedicated to R&D across data, software, and hardware. In 2024, the company filed 12 patents, highlighting its commitment to proprietary technologies. Tractian plans to expand its portfolio of patented solutions in 2025 while attracting top-tier talent in engineering, data science, and go-to-market teams. 1. Siemens Research. "The Impact of Downtime on Industrial Productivity." About Tractian Tractian is the Industrial Copilot for manufacturing leaders, with a platform that empowers businesses to prevent unplanned downtime, boost operational efficiency, and enhance maintenance capacity. The company is headquartered in Atlanta, GA, and extends its presence globally with offices in Mexico City and Sao Paulo. Learn more at tractian.com. About Sapphire Sapphire is a global software venture capital firm with more than $10 billion in AUM and team members across Austin, London, Menlo Park and San Francisco. For over a decade, Sapphire has partnered with visionary management teams and venture funds to back companies of consequence. Since its founding, Sapphire has invested in more than 170 companies globally resulting in more than 30 Public Listings and 45 acquisitions. The firm’s investment strategies - Sapphire Ventures, Sapphire Partners and Sapphire Sport - are focused on scaling companies and venture funds, elevating them to become category leaders. Sapphire’s Portfolio Growth team of experienced operators delivers a strategic blend of value-add services, tools and resources designed to support portfolio company leaders as they scale.
